articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA contractors accidentally turned GitHub into a government secret-sharing platform, because apparently the agency tasked with protecting our infrastructure needed a lesson in basic OpSec. Congressional lawmakers are rightfully losing their minds over this AWS GovCloud key leak.

articles.title: Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised to Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Anthropic's Claude Mythos AI just found 10,000 critical vulnerabilities in major software, proving that artificial intelligence is better at finding bugs than humans are at writing secure code. The robots aren't taking over yet, but they're definitely pointing out how terrible we are at cybersecurity.

articles.title: mempalace-dashboard added to PyPI
articles.summary: CVE-2026-48172 in LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin scores a perfect 10.0 CVSS because it lets attackers run arbitrary scripts as root. It's being actively exploited, which means someone's having a very bad day in hosting land.

articles.title: Cisco used AI to write security incident reports, with mixed results
articles.summary: Trump Mobile's website was allegedly leaking customer data to anyone who could craft an HTTP request, because why bother with authentication when you can just hand out personal info like campaign flyers. The irony of a 'law and order' candidate running a lawless data operation is *chef's kiss*.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a rare victory for end-to-end encryption, reminding us that keeping our digital conversations away from government voyeurs is still possible. In a world of surveillance capitalism, encrypted messaging remains our digital equivalent of whispering in a crowded room.

articles.title: Akamai Joins Growing Chorus of Vendors Betting Big on Secure Enterprise Browsers
articles.summary: EFF's new guide tackles the normalization of digital surveillance abuse across the Americas, because apparently we need step-by-step instructions to remember that mass surveillance is bad. Sometimes the obvious needs to be stated loudly for the people in the back.

articles.title: Claude Mythos AI Finds 10,000 High-Severity Flaws in Widely Used Software
articles.summary: Eight Packagist packages got poisoned with Linux malware hosted on GitHub, proving that supply chain attacks are the gift that keeps on giving. The attackers cleverly avoided composer.json, because why use the obvious attack vector when you can be sneaky about it.

articles.title: Companies Using Anthropic's Mythos AI Uncover 10K+ Serious Software Bugs
articles.summary: TeamPCP is conducting an unprecedented poisoning spree of open source code, with GitHub as their latest victim in a supply chain attack campaign that's impacting hundreds of organizations. When the foundation of modern software development becomes the attack vector, we're all screwed.

articles.title: Google API Keys Remain Active After Deletion
articles.summary: China's Webworm APT group is using Discord and Microsoft Graph APIs to hack EU governments, because why develop custom C2 infrastructure when Microsoft will host it for you. The irony of using American platforms to spy on European governments is deliciously twisted.

articles.title: AIPAC, AI, Crypto, and Gambling Are Hiding Their Big Election Spends
articles.summary: A federal judge sanctioned private prison giant CoreCivic for destroying video evidence in an ICE detainee death case, marking the first known sanction of its kind. Nothing says 'we're totally innocent' like systematically destroying evidence of your deadly negligence.
